solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Songbird died, old, in a flash

indicators.note: 'in' places the preceding pair of words inside the word for a sudden flash

blocks.note: OB, short for obiit, marks a death
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a blink is a flash of light or an instant

explanation.surface: A bird expires, aged, in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobolink is an American songbird of the blackbird family, named from its call.

clue.text: What Gandhi was for many, soul fully soaring

indicators.note: in a down entry, soaring means rising up the column, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: the ba is the soul in ancient Egyptian belief
up as in 'eaten up', meaning completely

explanation.surface: Gandhi's soul rose fully to the heavens in the eyes of his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The ba was the Egyptian soul-bird; 'up' for 'fully' is the sense in 'drink up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bapu, meaning father in Gujarati, was the affectionate title many Indians gave Gandhi.

clue.text: Plant with medicinal properties? Yellow nettle also reared

indicators.note: reared means raised up, and in a down entry a raised word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
to nettle is to annoy or anger
too means also

explanation.surface: A yellow-flowered nettle grown for its healing powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow nettle' looks like the plant name; the colour is the heraldic tincture and the nettle is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange-root is goldenseal, a North American herb whose root was used in folk medicine.

clue.text: Misleading prophet, repeatedly accepted in soothing stuff

indicators.note: 'in' puts the doubled letter inside the word for a soothing ointment

blocks.note: balm is a soothing ointment
A for accepted, given twice

explanation.surface: A false prophet keeps being welcomed into a comforting embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaam, the Old Testament seer, counselled the Moabites to lure Israel into sin, so he is a prophet who led people astray.

clue.text: A threat to e.g. lettuces, top topped?

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the climax is the top or peak

explanation.surface: Something menacing salad crops, with its head cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Limax is the genus of garden slugs, notorious pests that eat lettuces and other leafy plants.

clue.text: Fine pottery from Italy, found near the sea, timeless

indicators.note: 'timeless' means without time, so that word is struck out of the seaside one

blocks.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
maritime means by or of the sea

explanation.surface: Delicate ceramics from a seaside Italian town, ageless in style.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Italian pottery, but Imari ware is Japanese; Italy supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a Japanese porcelain, richly decorated, named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Airborne car, not once requiring a battery internally

indicators.note: 'internally' says the battery phrase goes inside the archaic negative

blocks.note: ne is an old word for not
a cell is a single battery

explanation.surface: A flying vehicle that never once needed a battery inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the basket or gondola slung beneath a balloon or airship, so a car that flies.

clue.text: Limestone once universal in English river

indicators.note: 'in' places the single letter inside the name of the river

blocks.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Limestone that was formerly found throughout an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the word as obsolete; it belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Caum is an obsolete spelling of cam, an old word for a kind of limestone or pipeclay.

clue.text: Co. furor unusually involving Britain – one's inclination changes

indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged
'involving' means taking in, so the country's letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is a standard abbreviation for Britain or British

explanation.surface: A company's outrage, oddly bound up with Britain, keeps shifting its slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the definition's subject: a roof whose inclination changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb-roof, or mansard, has two different slopes on each side, so its pitch alters partway down.

clue.text: What may afflict US patients? Nurse holding employees up

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the nurse word wraps the other piece
in a down entry, 'up' means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: aia, or ayah, is an Indian nursemaid
workers are a firm's men

explanation.surface: A nurse wonders what ails American patients while supporting her staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemia is the American spelling of anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells, hence 'US patients'.

clue.text: Tram rides off course, not right? Valued wrongly

indicators.note: a vehicle off course has strayed from its route, so the letters wander from their order
'not' says the following letter is left out of the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Tram journeys that leave the route and go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrate is to assess or estimate wrongly, so misrated means given the wrong value.

clue.text: A Muslim leader almost unravelled the soul of the cosmos? (10, two words)

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its other form
an imam leads prayers in a mosque
to unravel a knot is to undo it

explanation.surface: A cleric nearly comes apart pondering the spirit of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Anima mundi is Latin for 'world soul', the philosophical idea of a single animating spirit in all nature.

clue.text: Webbing one attached to a lamp that's broken

indicators.note: a broken object is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: Netting fixed to a smashed light fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A palama is the membrane joining the toes of a water bird's foot, the webbing of a duck.

clue.text: Salad garnish? Set removed from iron baskets

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so those letters go from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
cressets are iron baskets holding fire as beacons

explanation.surface: Is a salad decoration a set lifted from wire baskets?
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a peppery sprouting plant scattered on salads and sandwiches as a garnish.

clue.text: Cabinet moment to withdraw, active within

indicators.note: 'within' sends the single letter inside the word for withdraw

blocks.note: a sec is a moment
to retire is to withdraw
A is the abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A government minister's time to step down while still busy inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests the government; it is the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with drawers and shelves, a piece of cabinet furniture.

clue.text: One in sunwear that's slipped, oblivious

indicators.note: 'in' puts the single letter among the clothing word's letters
something that has slipped is out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose beachwear has slipped, quite unaware of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unawares means without knowing or noticing, as in 'caught unawares', so taken in an unknowing state.

clue.text: Small bit of film viewed – it's used for cutting

blocks.note: a frame is a single picture on a reel of film
saw means viewed

explanation.surface: A short clip was watched, and it was a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests film editing, but the definition is a woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame saw is a thin blade held taut in a frame, a tool for sawing wood.

clue.text: Philippic boosting assistance set before family

indicators.note: boosting means lifting up, which in a down entry reads the word bottom to top
'set before' puts the first piece ahead of the second

blocks.note: aid means assistance
a tribe is a family group

explanation.surface: A tirade boosting help given to a clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A philippic, after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon, is a bitter tirade or denunciation.

clue.text: Crumbs I caught acting in cuirass

blocks.note: Lor! is a dated exclamation of surprise, like Crumbs!
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: An actor exclaims at being caught on stage in armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorica was the Roman leather or metal breastplate, the same armour piece as a cuirass.

clue.text: Rand suffering seism, not at all vigorous

indicators.note: something suffering is damaged and knocked about, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: R is the symbol for the South African rand
taken as written

explanation.surface: The South African currency is hit by an earthquake and goes limp.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or slack, lacking energy and care in doing one's duty.

clue.text: Radio tuning somewhat rocky round big city being turned up

indicators.note: 'round' says the rocky word surrounds the city's letters
turned up in a down entry means flipped to read upwards

blocks.note: stony means full of stones, rocky in some measure
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Radio reception goes rather rocky around New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntony is the tuning of two radio circuits to resonate at the same frequency.

clue.text: Abrasive swine, cross?

blocks.note: a boar is a male pig
a T is cross-shaped

explanation.surface: A rude pig, and an angry one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' and 'cross' look like descriptions of a rude, angry person; one is the definition, the other a letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Boart is low-grade diamond fragments, crushed and used as an industrial grinding material.

clue.text: A prince accepts his father hanging?

indicators.note: 'accepts' means takes in, so the prince's title holds the other letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a ras is an Ethiopian prince
a prince's father is the king, R for rex

explanation.surface: A prince accepts his father's execution?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' suggests a death sentence; it is a tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry wall hanging, named after the French town where such cloth was woven.

clue.text: Kid still crawling, Arthur? Oddly good for husband (6, two words)

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means X takes Y's place, so one letter is swapped for another
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are put in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Is little Arthur still on all fours? Strangely good, for a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug rat is slang for a toddler, a child small enough to be crawling on the floor.

clue.text: Long poem poet penned in Early English

indicators.note: penned in means shut inside, so the poet goes inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English
Alexander Pope, the Augustan poet

explanation.surface: An epic composed by a poet in an archaic form of English.
explanation.definitionFit: An epopee is an epic poem, or epic poetry in general, from the Greek for epic-making.

clue.text: One with splendid hat in story, normal to behold

definitions.text: One with splendid hat in story

blocks.note: par is the normal or standard level
to see is to behold

explanation.surface: A storybook figure in a grand hat, quite ordinary to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: A Parsee is an Indian Zoroastrian; the reference is to Kipling's 'How the Rhinoceros Got His Skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's Just So story of the rhinoceros, a Parsee wears a hat that reflects the sun in more-than-oriental splendour.

clue.text: Scottish speaker introducing fashion for faux fur?

indicators.note: 'introducing' means coming before, so the first piece leads the second

blocks.note: mou is Scots for mouth, the organ of speech
ton means the prevailing fashion

explanation.surface: A Scot introduces a fashion for fake fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' suggests a person talking; it is the part of the body that speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouton is sheepskin sheared and dyed to imitate beaver or seal, hence an imitation fur.

clue.text: Salad served up – daughter introduced Scottish dyes

indicators.note: served up in a down entry means presented upwards, read bottom to top
'introduced' means brought in, so that letter goes inside

blocks.note: slaw is a cabbage salad
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A salad is served, and the daughter is brought into the colouring business.
explanation.definitionFit: Wald is the Scots form of weld, a plant yielding yellow dye, so walds are plant dyes.

clue.text: Venomous snake? It's kept under inverted box

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word reads from the bottom
in a down entry, kept under means placed below the preceding piece

blocks.note: an ark is a chest or box, like the Ark of the Covenant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisonous snake that someone keeps in an upturned box.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer key prints FREIT (a Scots omen), but the wordplay can only give KRAIT. Its middle letter crosses 31-across, which gives the same A.
explanation.definitionFit: A krait is a highly venomous South Asian snake related to the cobras.

clue.text: Unusual stage device to get discussion going (8, two words)

blocks.note: to get a talk going is to start a rap, rap being slang for a discussion

explanation.surface: A clever theatrical trick to open a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase START RAP, 'get discussion going', is re-spaced to make the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A star trap is a trapdoor of hinged triangular flaps that shoots an actor up onto the stage, a rare piece of machinery.

clue.text: Hide in shower

blocks.note: first meaning: an animal's skin
second meaning: to bombard

explanation.surface: Take cover in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an animal skin with its fur, and also as a verb to rain blows or missiles on someone.

clue.text: Spire in parts of the south, just right in the middle

definitions.text: Spire in parts of the south

indicators.note: 'in the middle' tells the solver to take the central letters of the phrase

blocks.note: the central letters of these two words, losing the outer two of each

explanation.surface: A church spire in a southern region that is centred just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of the south' marks a dialect word, not letters; 'spire' is the plant sense, not a steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: Strig is a southern English dialect word for a stalk, and spire is an old word for a shoot or stalk.

clue.text: Poet's slovenly, to decide on retiring that is

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: to seal a deal is to settle or decide on it
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A poet is too slack to settle on going to bed, that is.
explanation.walkthrough: The key prints LEASIE, but the wordplay gives LAESIE, Spenser's own spelling. 'Poet's' marks the word as Spenserian.
explanation.definitionFit: Laesie is Spenser's spelling of lazy, so the 'poet's' word for idle or sluggish.

clue.text: A musical group and how it stands, for rock of a kind?

indicators.note: 'and how it stands' frames the group: a band standing is set within a straight row

blocks.note: a band on stage stands in a line
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A musical group and its stance, all for a kind of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' wants to be the music a band plays; it is a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabandine is an old name for a deep red garnet or manganese mineral from Alabanda in Asia Minor, a kind of stone.

clue.text: The old know what youth twigs eventually – they're only beginners

indicators.note: only the beginners means just the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: surface padding that labels the defined word as archaic
the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Elders know what the young eventually realise, since the young are only novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the word as archaic; 'twigs' here is slang for understands.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyte is an archaic form meaning to know, kin to wit and wot.

clue.text: No major thoroughfare – bet tyre's getting damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Avoid the main road: tyres are bound to be ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystreet is a minor side street off the main roads, so not a major route.
